task.description: Implement the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved (PASS, rework iteration 1, re-gate PASS) fix design at lib/letflow/design/iss0400-nested-parallel-gateway-fix.md in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex. The design specifies: collect_leaf_gateways/3's step-4 PARALLEL_GATEWAY clause now dispatches on gateway_role/2's existing classification -- :join/:pass_through keeps today's immediate-terminal body byte-for-byte unchanged (this is load-bearing: it is what keeps ISS-0398's own fix, and every one of its existing fixtures, unaffected); :split routes to a new private function resolve_nested_split/3, which resolves the nested split via the SAME leaf_search_state() the outer walk is already threading -- explicitly NOT resetting stack/stack_set/index/lowlink/next_index at this boundary (this was the exact mechanism that failed the design gate once at BLOCKER severity for causing infinite recursion; the design's final, twice-validated version shares state fully instead), then continues the walk from the inner join's own outgoing edge once resolved. Implement exactly what the design specifies -- read it in full, including the worked traces in sections 3.2 and the exact @spec given for resolve_nested_split/3. Do not deviate from the design's stated mechanism (particularly: do not reintroduce any reset of Tarjan bookkeeping at the resolve_nested_split/3 boundary -- that is precisely the defect the design gate caught and reworked away). If anything in the design turns out to be mechanically infeasible against real Elixir/the real existing code (the same class of finding that triggered ISS-0392's own design rework), report it honestly rather than forcing something that doesn't actually work, and flag it in your result rather than silently improvising a different mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: collect_leaf_gateways/3's PARALLEL_GATEWAY dispatch matches the design's :join/:pass_through vs :split branching exactly, with the :join/:pass_through path unchanged from current behavior
resolve_nested_split/3 is implemented per the design's @spec and does not reset stack/stack_set/index/lowlink/next_index at its own boundary
Existing test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs suite still passes unchanged (non-regression of ISS-0398's own fix)
No changes outside lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex unless the design explicitly requires them

result.summary: Implemented the twice-validated design exactly. collect_leaf_gateways/3's %Node{node_type: :PARALLEL_GATEWAY} arm now dispatches on gateway_role/2: :join/:pass_through is byte-for-byte the prior body (immediate terminal, memoized, no stack push -- ISS-0398's fix and fixtures untouched); :combined_unsupported folds into :dead_end (memoized under its own node_id, consistent with the other terminal cases in this function); :split now pushes the nested-split node onto the shared Tarjan stack exactly like explore_branching_node/3 does for an ordinary node (this was necessary and matches the design's own worked traces at lines 471-472/522-524, which show 'inner_split' assigned an index and pushed before resolve_nested_split/3 is entered -- the design's prose in §2.3 focuses on 'no reset', not 'no push', and the traces make the push explicit) and then calls the new resolve_nested_split/3. resolve_nested_split/3 folds over the nested split's own outgoing edges via the existing fold_outgoing_edges/4 (reused verbatim per design open-questions 1/4, not reimplemented), threading the exact same state with zero resets of memo/index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index. On singleton agreement it resolves the inner join's own outgoing edge and recurses collect_leaf_gateways/3 on that target (continuing past the inner join, never stopping at it); on disagreement/no-agreement it folds to :dead_end. Either way the SCC closure decision (pop-and-memoize vs. stay open/propagate {:open, lowlink}) is made by reusing close_scc_or_defer/5 -- fed the *continuation-resolved* leaves (or :dead_end) rather than the fold's own raw leaves, which is what makes memo[gw_node.id] correctly 'see through' the nested split (design line 496-497) instead of caching the nested split's own id. Traced both worked examples in the design (§3.2's non-cyclic trace and its cyclic ancestor-back-edge counterexample trace) by hand against the final implementation node-by-node/index-by-index and both match exactly, including the {:open, 0} propagation for 'inner_split' in the cyclic case and the correct three-member SCC close at 'A'. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, 'Compiling 3 files (.ex)', no warnings. mix format --check-formatted: clean, no output. mix test test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs: 'Result: 12 passed', 0 failures -- no regression of ISS-0398's own fixtures. mix test test/letflow/engine/ (full directory, run synchronously to completion): 'Result: 898 passed (1 property, 897 tests), 7 excluded' -- 0 failures, including the process_instance_test.exs property test. No files changed outside lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex (plus this handoff). One deviation from a literal first reading of the design worth flagging explicitly per the task's own instruction to report infeasibility honestly, though it turned out feasible: the design's §2.3 prose alone (read before the worked traces) could be misread as leaving the nested-split node itself unpushed onto the Tarjan stack, the way a :join/:pass_through PARALLEL_GATEWAY never is -- but both worked traces in §3.2 explicitly show the nested-split node ("inner_split") assigned a Tarjan index and pushed onto stack/stack_set before resolve_nested_split/3 is ever entered, and the closure check at the end (local_lowlink == own_index) only makes sense against that pushed index. I implemented it per the traces (which the design doc states are load-bearing and re-derived, not merely illustrative) rather than the more ambiguous prose-only reading, and hand-verified both traces node-by-node against the final code to confirm this reading is correct and matches iteration 2's twice-validated mechanism.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (tenant-data path: touches Letflow.Engine.Transition's gateway-dispatch/leaf-lookahead logic used at split-node activation for every tenant's workflow instances), then REVIEWER, per WF-03 Step 2a/2b-equivalent gates before TEST-DESIGNER.
